column7: Dual parallel fuzz and glitch design with separate fuzz and glitch controls. The fuzz section uses Volume, Gain, Sens and Kill; the glitch section uses Drift and Depth with Amok/Drone modes. The two processing paths run in parallel and mix at the output. 2023 coverage identifies the builder as Icelandic.
column10: Strong identification markers are the dual parallel architecture, separate glitch footswitch, Amok/Drone modes and the Kill/Gain/Sens/Volume/Drift/Depth control family. Preserve later V2 evidence separately from the 2023 product identity.

column7: Redbeard's first dedicated fuzz pedal, using a three-way clipping selector for Silicone, LED and Germanium modes. Fully analogue, true bypass, and hand designed, engineered, built, tested and packaged in the UK.
column10: The three clipping modes and explicit first-dedicated-fuzz status are strong identification markers. Keep later builder products separate from this first dedicated fuzz entry.

column7: Analogue octave-up fuzz with digitally controlled switching and Octapulse tremolo/vibrato. Four main controls are Volume, Tone, Mix and Fuzz, with Voice and Mode controls, external control/tap functions and multiple operating modes. Released in December 2023 after about three years of development.
column10: Preserve the analogue audio path and digital control layer, Octapulse behavior, Voice/Mode system and external control architecture as identification evidence. Do not infer a later generation from firmware or documentation revisions alone.

column7: Modern Fuzz Face collaboration using matched NKT/CV7351 germanium transistors, external Bias, a Xen transformer/unbuffering switch and Morph control. The circuit originated as a larger custom Hello Sailor build and was then adapted and standardised by rnrmf guitarworks for repeatable production in Australia.
column10: This is a relationship-rich record: distinguish the original custom HSE build, the rnrmf standardised production collaboration, and later cosmetic specimens. Xen/Morph controls and the collaboration names are high-value specimen clues.

column7: 2023 coverage documents a compact silicon multi-fuzz using four selected transistors with switchable Fuzz Face, Maestro and Tone Bender-family voicings. Controls include Bass, Mid Cut, Treble, Volume, Bias, Gain and Impedance, plus a family selector.
column10: Treat V2 as the documented product label, not proof of a particular circuit redesign. The control density and voicing selector are strong identification clues pending primary Bispell documentation.

column7: Highly expanded Fuzz Face/Rangemaster platform with A/B gain and bias controls, Ge/Si transistor options, pickup simulator, boost and range controls. 2023 coverage identifies both a feature-dense V2 and a streamlined Green Edition.
column10: Keep Solarist V2 and Green Edition as distinct variant/edition states. Do not collapse the extensive switchable transistor and Rangemaster functions into a generic Fuzz Face identity.

column7: Three-control Fuzz Face interpretation using two Micro Electronics C1016Y yellow-dot silicon transistors, adding Tone to the usual Volume and Fuzz layout. Hand built in Northamptonshire with screen-printed enclosure artwork.
column10: The C1016Y yellow-dot transistor specification, three-control layout and hand screen-printed enclosure are strong specimen clues. Keep Facet IZ distinct from Facet FF, the more faithful 1969 reproduction.

column7: Custom Shop limited Octaurus using a batch of early-1960s NOS silicon transistors, turret point-to-point construction, olive-drab suede enclosure, Level/Tone/Gain and two voicing/clipping toggles. The limited run sold out and was followed by separate standard and NOS Octaurus identities.
column10: Clean edition boundary: preserve the limited Custom Shop construction, NOS sourcing and suede/see-through-bottom enclosure as distinct from later standard and NOS products.
